pairs.question: Legatum mihi obvenit modicum sed amplissimo gratius. Cur amplissimo gratius?
pairs.answer: Pomponia Galla exheredato filio Asudio Curiano heredem reliquerat me, dederat coheredes Sertorium Severum praetorium virum aliosque splendidos equites Romanos.
pairs.derivation: Pliny poses his own question 'Cur amplissimo gratius?' after the statement that the legacy was more welcome than a very large one; the preceding sentence is kept as verbatim setup so 'amplissimo gratius' has its referent. The answer is the first explanatory sentence naming Pomponia Galla's bequest; it stops at the first full stop, before 'Curianus orabat...', where the narrative turns from explaining why the legacy was gratifying to recounting Curianus's request.
